sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Botany, who listens for hope amid the blizzard, relays your signal to places farther still.

Silence, like mediocrity, carries a sin of its own.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A foldable miniature antenna — or is it a hairpin? Botany handed it to you without a word of explanation, just a sly little smile.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Botany, born Tishina Viktorovna Belyaeva, attended the Imperial Polytechnic University in Deity Grypherburg but did not graduate. She joined Rhodes Island on the recommendation of Operator Zima, where she continues to study and research Originium communication technology while also taking part in field operations.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Botany shows no signs of Oripathy.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.11u/L
Operator Botany maintains a strong awareness of Oripathy protection protocols.

Operator Botany once 'modified' her right horn on her own, embedding a metal antenna to improve her ability to receive communication signals. Testing and analysis by the Medical Department confirm that the procedure caused no damage to her nervous system, but the defect at the junction and the strain the metal places on her cervical spine remain points of concern going forward.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Tishina Viktorovna Belyaeva is not the first name Botany ever used, but it is the one that has stayed with her the longest.
The certificates pasted on the wall, the yellowed photograph set in a jeweled frame, and the thick stack of disciplinary notices all faithfully record the important moments Tishina has lived through.
For a long time, Tishina believed that it was sheer luck that had gotten her into the Imperial Polytechnic University in Deity Grypherburg, and that had placed that generous scholarship in her hands from Grand Duchess Yelisaveta herself. Afterwards, the Grand Duchess sent someone to invite her into that solemn building. What she could not understand was that, in the end, she simply stood there, watching from a distance as the Grand Duchess conversed with several aides. She waited an hour beside the warm hearth, and the Grand Duchess never once looked her way. Only when she stepped back out of that building did she realize how cold it was outside.
The Imperial Polytechnic University was not the wonderful place Tishina had imagined. It was the famed 'Garden of Nobility,' where the great and powerful deposited their unmanageable children for a few years in that magnificent school and had them emerge transformed into 'distinguished intellectuals.' In a place like that, there was never going to be room for a commoner Elafia from Bresk. It was difficult even to find a handful of students there who were not Ursus. Tishina was often locked out of her dormitory late at night by her classmates, or spent her early mornings searching for shoes and scarves that had 'mysteriously vanished.'
为了减少麻烦，季申娜干脆在全天开放的图书馆找了个储藏间住进去。这为她博来了“书呆子”的外号，但也让她终于拥有了一片清净之地。她曾在图书馆里翻到一本写着“科谢尼娅·马尔科芙娜·涅留朵娃”名字的笔记，那似乎是一位非乌萨斯学生写下的生存指南。尽管时过境迁，笔记上的一些地点和人名都已发生变化乃至消失，但季申娜还是从中汲取到了自己所需要的勇气。书本是更称职的老师，她照着专业教科书中的指引，制作出了自己一直想要的通讯装置，她甚至还改造了自己的犄角，只为能听见更远处传来的讯号……
Then, on that night, everything changed.
The roars and wails from the Far North drowned her. She tried to tell others everything she had heard, only to find that she had no capacity to make a sound at all. Without a voice, she could bring about no change. Listening to the sounds carried from the Far North, feeling the snowflakes cut into her skin, she finally understood why the Grand Duchess had summoned her that day, only to leave her standing off to one side.
It was such a simple thing, and no different from the reason she had been admitted to that school reserved for the nobility—the Grand Duchess needed a gifted child of humble birth like her, to showcase her own benevolence and compassion. All Tishina had to do was be seen: seen by the onlookers in the street, walking into the Grand Duchess's building and staying there for a little over an hour. And then the people would say, look how merciful and gracious our Grand Duchess is. What she had taken for the fruits of her effort and her good fortune turned out to be nothing more than a political performance arranged in advance.
After that night, Tishina's name began to appear again and again on the school's disciplinary notices, while 'Botany'—the nickname first coined to mock her—began to spread among the students who were trying to speak up about the tragedy in the Far North.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Once things had settled down, Botany finally met Mantra and Raidian at Rhodes Island, and got the microphone signed by Raidian herself that she had always wanted. After learning that operators from Mantra's squad sometimes hold open lectures on the efficient use of long-range communication Originium Arts, Botany began spending her free time in the Engineering Department's sharing room, hoping to catch one of the sessions.

I actually got a great deal out of those sessions. Everyone seemed unfamiliar with one another, all sitting far apart. I am not good at remembering faces, so at first I did not dare walk up and greet colleagues I did not recognize. I could not even tell who was a 'lecturer' and who was a 'student.'
不过幸好，这样尴尬的状况没持续多久。某天我刚修理完头顶的天线，讲师们便主动来考我。不得不说，那些问题还真的挺有难度，有的我答不上来，讲师们也会流露出失望的神色——从那以后，我常常在宿舍熬夜钻研，尽量跟上他们的节奏。我应该……表现得还可以，也确实受益于这种独特的教学方式，我学到了很多新知识。
If anything surprised me, it was that the lecturers seemed to far outnumber the students who came to listen—and for some reason, they always singled me out for questions.
—Operator Botany

I went to Engineering's sharing room too! I always thought the irregular sessions held by the seniors of Mantra's squad were just a legend, but they turned out to be real!
Senior Botany doesn't seem to like talking much, so for the first two sessions we all just sat there awkwardly, and nobody dared step up to ask anything. Then one day, the antenna on her head suddenly started swaying—I knew that meant she was urging us to ask questions, so I worked up the nerve and went for it!
Senior Botany's Ursus accent left a deep impression on me. She speaks unhurriedly and steadily, and very methodically. Sometimes, when I asked a sloppy question, she would stop right there and make me think it through myself, so I would go back to my quarters and study all night, and only the next day would she give me the correct answer. In just a few weeks, the other rookie operators who had just joined Engineering and I all felt that our technical and theoretical skills had improved enormously. We even co-signed a letter of appreciation and sent it to Senior Mantra, to thank her and the operators of her squad for helping us!
—A certain Engineering operator

Ah—no wonder nobody ever came to the sessions I held. Everyone was going to the sharing room! And here I've been waiting for you all in the break room this whole time!
Isn't hashing out academic problems in the break room the Engineering Department's whole style? Or have I had it wrong this whole time?
算了，不要紧。先把这封感谢信藏好，可别被队长发现了……什么叫信是队长让你转交给我的？她已经知道了？！
—Operator Elysium

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
Tishina Viktorovna Belyaeva is the name Botany has used the longest, but it is not her first.
Her first name came from the rime and the spring water of Sami; she says it cannot be translated into any other language. It was the name her elder sister gave her.
When she spoke the word 'sister,' the light in Botany's eyes suddenly dimmed.
姐姐和她完全不像，甚至也不像她们的母亲。某天姐姐说要带她去看冰泉，却将她独自留在了覆雪的林地中。她一遍遍呼唤着姐姐的名字，恐惧地在地上掘出浅浅的土坑，试图将自己藏起来……她不知道自己在黑暗的密林里待了多久，记忆似乎从那里断开了。后来某一次围坐在火堆旁时，姐姐对妹妹说，其实姐姐当时就在不远处看着她。“那你为什么不回应我？”她向姐姐发问。姐姐说，因为她发音不准，始终没能叫对姐姐的名字。她记得自己曾看向姐姐的眼睛，却只看到了“失望”。

After I was left behind in the forest that time, my sister gave me a walkie-talkie she had made herself. She taught me how to tune it to a special channel, how to call into it, and how to receive an answer.
I was far too young then to understand what my sister was doing. Mother may have noticed something, but she never wanted to bring it up with me.
I still remember the day we moved away from Sami. As we walked, my sister suddenly stopped. She said, 'This is as far as I go.'
She was still speaking Sami. She said she could only see Mother and me this far. I wanted to go with her, but she refused—she said that now that I had an Ursus name, I could not go back with her anymore. Mother said nothing at all, and only wept.
I remember I was holding the walkie-talkie my sister gave me, and I recalled how, whenever I could not find her before, all I had to do was call her name on that channel and she would appear in time and tell me which sound I had gotten wrong this time.
So I switched the walkie-talkie on, and suddenly did not know what to call out—I could not remember her Sami name at all, as though everything about Sami were vanishing from my head at speed. In my panic, I called out the Ursus name that would stay with me for many years to come.
My sister did not stop. She disappeared into the snow. Perhaps, if I had called out the right name with the right pronunciation, she would have stayed? I do not know.
I lost that walkie-talkie afterwards. Perhaps Mother threw it away on purpose. I have wanted another one ever since.
—A self-narrated recording from a psychological counseling session; Operator Botany has consented to Human Resources accessing this file

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
In the aftermath of the 'Katorga Incident,' Rhodes Island took in a steady stream of those who had lived through it, seeking to help them out of their psychological difficulties.
Of those who eventually became Rhodes Island operators, Botany was the most cooperative, and the first to consent to using the 'In Vivo Exposure Trauma Recording Self-Therapy Device, Type β' and to syncing her session records with the Medical Department.
Frankly, her air of 'it doesn't matter' is decidedly abnormal—that was the Medical Department's preliminary assessment of Botany.

[Audio Log]
(Electronic static)
……吗？嗯，好像又有电磁干扰。刚才说的那些内容应该都录制上了吧？
坏消息是，我没找到停止录制并保存的按钮，也不敢随便拆解这台机器。但好消息是，电量还有2%，它没电关机前应该会自动保存……的吧？那就再说一会儿好了。我是怎么被关进封锁区，怎么和索尼娅她们一起逃出来的，都原原本本地告诉你们了。剩下的，还有什么可以说的呢？
难道真的要讲讲，我是怎么在衣柜里躲了两三天，用只有自己能听见的声音向外求救吗？不……又或者要讲讲……我是怎么夺走别人的生命的……
(Heavy breathing)
不……不。
我不是……故意的。至少，杀第一个人的时候，不是。他当时……挥着刀，好像感觉不到痛一样。
我只是想……活下去。我不想再躲在那个衣柜里，那个衣柜的门板背面，全是带血的抓痕……在我躲进去前，就已经有人死在那里了。
没人能听见我，我做的一切都没有用……卡托加区，是一具……给活人的棺材。
(Violent retching)
……对不起。
How am I supposed to delete this recording?
人们在死去……我为什么还在这里自言自语？
No, this isn't right—
(Recording ends)

Botany submitted this recording of her own accord. She admitted that she had failed to keep her emotions in check, which led to the accidental destruction of the 'In Vivo Exposure Trauma Recording Self-Therapy Device, Type β,' and that she was only able to recover the surviving portion of the recording from its storage unit.
和录音文件一起提交的还有一柄折断的匕首。伯塔尼说，这是她从那个藏身的衣柜里带出来的，她不清楚这柄匕首曾属于谁，是否是用来自保的武器，也不愿去猜想那个人最后结局如何。当时她带走这柄折断的匕首只是出于一种朦胧的责任感，带着这份“责任”，她活了下来，却始终不敢回头去看。她的原话是“就像落枕一样，一旦回过头去，会很痛，很痛，但总会不痛的，只是时间问题。现在我的时间到了，我感觉自己可以放下它了。不过……我不知道该交给谁，你们愿意收下吗？”

Also, I would like to ask about the intellectual property status of the 'In Vivo Exposure Trauma Recording Self-Therapy Device, Type β.' I tried to repair it, but never managed to. I have now built some small recording devices modeled on its core structure, and I wanted to ask whether I need to pay Miss Closure a licensing fee in a case like this. Rest assured, I will only use them to record diaries. In my earlier sessions, I found this sort of talking to myself suited me rather well. At least I am making a sound. At least I can hear it.
—Operator Botany

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Tishina, my child, I hope all is well with you when this letter reaches you.
Thank you for telling me your new address and how you have been. It has eased this frightened heart of mine considerably.
家里没什么好担忧的，布列斯克的天气总是这样，但在这里我起码还能收到你的信，还能以合理的价格买到面粉和蔬菜，不是吗？至于你说的搬家，我考虑过，孩子，我真的考虑了很久。但很抱歉，我现在的地址是你姐姐仅有的关于我们俩的信息，我总是盼望着我的两个孩子都能平平安安地走进家门……季申娜，你会原谅妈妈吗？
你所说的罗德岛，我最近也和他们接触过了。他们人很好，只是个个都板着一副面孔，为了不被人怀疑，他们还特意换上了什么“第三局”的制服，真是辛苦他们了。他们每周都会来拜访我，给我带来一些食物和布料，顺便替你取走你留下的一些旧物件，上次他们来，还把你寄回的信件也带走了，说是为了保密必须销毁掉。虽然不知道你为什么要请他们把小时候从萨米带过来的玩具都寄去罗德岛……也许你还留着一些那里的记忆吧。对了，那些人还问我，你最近有没有跟你的老朋友联络过。可我又怎么知道呢？他们还特意写下了那位朋友的名字，好像怕我耳聋听不清一样，真是贴心。
Which reminds me, Tishina—when did you meet this young man 'Fedya'? What is he like? Why have you never mentioned him to me?
From your mother, who is dying to hear more about you and your 'old friend'
